The hypothetical change is that keys whose values are `None` remain present when request settings merge with session settings. The supplied evidence does not identify exact module or function locations, provide source lines, or establish runtime behavior.

## The merge rule is the central affected behavior

The relevant rule is the request-and-session-settings merge behavior that previously removed keys assigned `None`. Under the hypothetical change, a `None` value is preserved rather than treated as a signal to remove the key [Data: supplied query].

This means the merge result can retain an explicitly `None`-valued key. The supplied evidence does not specify whether this rule applies to every setting or only to selected settings.

The header/parameter call site is affected because it consumes settings produced by the request-and-session merge [Data: supplied query].

If the merge now preserves `None`-valued keys, that call site may receive those keys instead of receiving a mapping from which they were removed. The available evidence does not identify the module, function, parameter names, or exact statement responsible for this behavior.

The header/parameter and environment-setting call sites are both downstream of the request-and-session-settings merge behavior [Data: supplied query].
